title: Sordland/Turn04/InT_SSCRailwayIssue
description: Half of the first infrastructure project has been completed. But further progress has been halted due to an issue which the player must choose to solve in a way. Dependant on each corporation a different issue appears and all of them have different absolute solutions or failures leading to making the opening deadline or missing it by two months.

entries.speaker: START
entries.title: START

entries.title: input

entries.speaker: OUTPUT

entries.speaker: Narrator
entries.title: Narrator: "The main purpose of our visit was t..."
entries.dialogueText: The main purpose of our visit was to solve construction issues that began to endanger the deadline.

entries.speaker: Narrator
entries.title: Narrator: "The L-1 Railway construction create..."
entries.dialogueText: The L-1 Railway construction created the perfect opportunity to visit the green technological nerve centre of Sordland. Dozens of electrical engineers from the city were part of the electrification upgrade of the rail track.

entries.speaker: Narrator
entries.title: Narrator: "There was also a message of support..."
entries.dialogueText: There was also a message of support from the mayor of Anrica, Curtan Leste, who was grateful for the L-1 investments.

entries.speaker: Narrator
entries.title: Narrator: "The Gelsord Research Council was ve..."
entries.dialogueText: The Gelsord Research Council was very willing to let us use their facilities because the rectors were pleased by the increase of the education funding.

entries.speaker: Narrator
entries.title: Narrator: "The Gelsord Research Council let us..."
entries.dialogueText: The Gelsord Research Council let us use their facilities, but the rectors weren't interested in our affairs.

entries.speaker: Narrator
entries.title: Narrator: "The Gelsord Research Council was ve..."
entries.dialogueText: The Gelsord Research Council was very reluctant to let us use their facilities as the rectors weren't at all pleased by the reduction of education funding.

entries.speaker: Narrator
entries.title: Narrator: "The meeting ended. The three of us..."
entries.dialogueText: The meeting ended. The three of us toured the Advanced Research and Development divisions in Gelsord.

entries.speaker: Narrator
entries.title: Narrator: "The day-long visit ended with a din..."
entries.dialogueText: The day-long visit ended with a dinner involving the most important people in the city. Many of them were scientists.

entries.speaker: Symon Holl
entries.title: Symon Holl: "“That should be it. Good that we ha..."
entries.dialogueText: “That should be it. Good that we have figured out a way to move the process forward.”

entries.speaker: Narrator
entries.title: Narrator: "Later, we made our way back to Hols..."
entries.dialogueText: Later, we made our way back to Holsord.

entries.speaker: Symon Holl
entries.title: GameCondition.Turn04_InT_Issue = true

entries.speaker: Narrator
entries.title: Narrator: "Symon looked a little more stressed..."
entries.dialogueText: Symon looked a little more stressed than usual. Gus was also here to find solutions. He eyed me for a while.

entries.speaker: Symon Holl
entries.title: Symon Holl: "“We scheduled the project to finish..."
entries.dialogueText: “We scheduled the project to finish in late 1955 but I have concerns about the construction due to progress being slower than expected.”

entries.speaker: Player
entries.title: Player: "“Do we have a case of project misma..."
entries.dialogueText: “Do we have a case of project mismanagement?”
entries.menuText: “Do we have a case of project mismanagement?”

entries.speaker: Player
entries.title: Player: "“Finding competent managers could w..."
entries.dialogueText: “Finding competent managers could work. New blood can move things back on track.”
entries.menuText: “Finding competent managers could work. New blood can move things back on track.”

entries.speaker: Gus Manger
entries.title: Gus Manger: "“I know many skilled and experience..."
entries.dialogueText: “I know many skilled and experienced people in the construction industry. So does Symon too, I presume.”

entries.speaker: Symon Holl
entries.title: Symon Holl: "“The warning will hopefully have a..."
entries.dialogueText: “The warning will hopefully have a positive result to their performance. We could escalate further later.”

entries.speaker: Player
entries.title: Player: "“The incompetent managers should be..."
entries.dialogueText: “The incompetent managers should be fired. This is a disgrace.”
entries.menuText: “The incompetent managers should be fired. This is a disgrace.”

entries.speaker: Symon Holl
entries.title: Symon Holl: "“It would be a drastic measure but..."
entries.dialogueText: “It would be a drastic measure but not unreasonable. Replacing them with competent managers would do.”

entries.speaker: Gus Manger
entries.title: Gus Manger: "“The shake-up could have a positive..."
entries.dialogueText: “The shake-up could have a positive result but what if the SSC overall boycotts against this.”

entries.speaker: Gus Manger
entries.title: Gus Manger: "“I will personally go and talk to a..."
entries.dialogueText: “I will personally go and talk to a few SSC managers and tell them of the gravity of the situation.”

entries.speaker: Symon Holl
entries.title: Symon Holl: "“I don't expect them to bite back b..."
entries.dialogueText: “I don't expect them to bite back but maybe they can further slow the construction by protesting.”

entries.speaker: Player
entries.title: Player: "“The state owns the SSC. They can't..."
entries.dialogueText: “The state owns the SSC. They can't retaliate and bite off the hand that feeds them.”
entries.menuText: “The state owns the SSC. They can't retaliate and bite off the hand that feeds them.”

entries.speaker: Narrator
entries.title: Narrator: "Symon took a deep breath and contin..."
entries.dialogueText: Symon took a deep breath and continued.

entries.speaker: Gus Manger
entries.title: Gus Manger: "“I say we replace them with more co..."
entries.dialogueText: “I say we replace them with more competent managers. It should help resolve the resources being handled inefficiently.”

entries.speaker: Symon Holl
entries.title: BaseGame.Turn04_InT_RailwayIssue_Solved = true

entries.speaker: Symon Holl
entries.title: Symon Holl: "“Couldn't agree more. This shouldn'..."
entries.dialogueText: “Couldn't agree more. This shouldn't keep going on any longer.”

entries.speaker: Symon Holl
entries.title: BaseGame.Turn04_InT_Issue_SSC_Replace = true; BaseGameSupport.Journal_Turn04_Infrastructure_SSCReplaced = true;

entries.speaker: Player
entries.title: Player: "“We can't let mismanagement delay t..."
entries.dialogueText: “We can't let mismanagement delay the project. It is unacceptable.”
entries.menuText: “We can't let mismanagement delay the project. It is unacceptable.”

entries.speaker: Player
entries.title: Player: "“Warn the construction managers. Se..."
entries.dialogueText: “Warn the construction managers. Send a formal warning from the Ministry of Economy and the Presidency.”
entries.menuText: “Warn the construction managers. Send a formal warning from the Ministry of Economy and the Presidency.”

entries.speaker: Gus Manger
entries.title: Gus Manger: "“State owned corporations like them..."
entries.dialogueText: “State owned corporations like them never really receive performance penalties and that's why they are incompetent and lack responsibility.”

entries.speaker: Player
entries.title: Player: "“Giving them a serious warning coul..."
entries.dialogueText: “Giving them a serious warning could be the solution. A slap on the wrist can do wonders.”
entries.menuText: “Giving them a serious warning could be the solution. A slap on the wrist can do wonders.”

entries.speaker: Player
entries.title: Player: "“Replace the construction managers..."
entries.dialogueText: “Replace the construction managers with more competent people to ensure the deadline is hit.”
entries.menuText: “Replace the construction managers with more competent people to ensure the deadline is hit.”

entries.speaker: Gus Manger
entries.title: Gus Manger: "“I'll make some calls. Got good con..."
entries.dialogueText: “I'll make some calls. Got good contacts that can be added to the potential candidates.”

entries.speaker: Symon Holl
entries.title: Symon Holl: "“It's good to see that failure isn'..."
entries.dialogueText: “It's good to see that failure isn't rewarded and punished. We will find more competent people through our networks.”

entries.speaker: Symon Holl
entries.title: Symon Holl: "“There is a good chance that they w..."
entries.dialogueText: “There is a good chance that they will take this far more seriously and take measures to increase speed.”

entries.speaker: Symon Holl
entries.title: Symon Holl: "“One of the important issues is the..."
entries.dialogueText: “One of the important issues is their construction management team. The other could be the outdated construction methods used which require more manpower, but we aren't sure if that contributes to the issue.”

entries.speaker: Player
entries.title: Player: "“How can we speed up the constructi..."
entries.dialogueText: “How can we speed up the construction to get back on track?”
entries.menuText: “How can we speed up the construction to get back on track?”

entries.speaker: Symon Holl
entries.title: BaseGame.Turn04_InT_Issue_SSC_Money = true; BaseGameSupport.Journal_Turn04_Infrastructure_SSCFunds = true;

entries.speaker: Symon Holl
entries.title: Symon Holl: "“That is the million ren question...."
entries.dialogueText: “That is the million ren question. There are a couple of issues that need to be resolved if we want the SSC to make the deadline.”

entries.speaker: Gus Manger
entries.title: Gus Manger: "“They aren't managing to maintain t..."
entries.dialogueText: “They aren't managing to maintain the speed of the construction with the resources given. Why should they receive more?”

entries.speaker: Player
entries.title: Player: "“The SSC might need more resources..."
entries.dialogueText: “The SSC might need more resources to speed things up. That deadline must be met.”
entries.menuText: “The SSC might need more resources to speed things up. That deadline must be met.”

entries.speaker: Symon Holl
entries.title: Symon Holl: "“A cash injection to hire more work..."
entries.dialogueText: “A cash injection to hire more workers and buy more machinery could have a positive effect on the construction.”

entries.speaker: Player
entries.title: Player: "“It might even be necessary for us..."
entries.dialogueText: “It might even be necessary for us to hit the opening date.”
entries.menuText: “It might even be necessary for us to hit the opening date.”

entries.speaker: Symon Holl
entries.title: Symon Holl: "“Let's hope that they handle the mo..."
entries.dialogueText: “Let's hope that they handle the money well. I'm still not a hundred percent sure about this.”

entries.speaker: Gus Manger
entries.title: Gus Manger: "“That is my theory because they kne..."
entries.dialogueText: “That is my theory because they knew about the zones the track passes by. The old SSC construction managers think they are untouchable and that they have no obligations.”

entries.speaker: Symon Holl
entries.title: Symon Holl: "“We can either give the constructio..."
entries.dialogueText: “We can either give the construction managers more money, warn them or replace them.”

entries.speaker: Symon Holl
entries.title: Symon Holl: "“One way or another we have to solv..."
entries.dialogueText: “One way or another we have to solve this issue. This can lead to real complications down the line otherwise.”

entries.speaker: Gus Manger
entries.title: Gus Manger: "“I think that chance is far more li..."
entries.dialogueText: “I think that chance is far more likely. I wouldn't take that risk if I were you because there are many more critical investments we can make.”

entries.speaker: Symon Holl
entries.title: BaseGame.Turn04_InT_Issue_SSC_Warn = true; BaseGameSupport.Journal_Turn04_Infrastructure_SSCWarning = true;

entries.speaker: Gus Manger
entries.title: Gus Manger: "“This proves that they have failed..."
entries.dialogueText: “This proves that they have failed at their base contractual agreement. What a shame that we trusted them.”

entries.speaker: Player
entries.title: Player: "“There is also the chance that the..."
entries.dialogueText: “There is also the chance that the money could be wasted. We already spent so much on this investment.”
entries.menuText: “There is also the chance that the money could be wasted. We already spent so much on this investment.”

entries.speaker: Player
entries.title: Player: "“Give more money to the constructio..."
entries.dialogueText: “Give more money to the construction managers so they can hire more workers and buy machinery to hit the deadline.”
entries.menuText: “Give more money to the construction managers so they can hire more workers and buy machinery to hit the deadline.” [-1 Government Budget]

entries.speaker: Symon Holl
entries.title: Symon Holl: "“This extra investment could be jus..."
entries.dialogueText: “This extra investment could be just enough to get things back on track. However, it is unfortunate we had to spend more because we need it elsewhere too.”

entries.speaker: Gus Manger
entries.title: Gus Manger: "“The SSC reported that they have be..."
entries.dialogueText: “The SSC reported that they have been slowed down due to several areas on the way to Gelsord having a potential for landslides that could endanger the workers. My argument is that they should have known about it.”

entries.speaker: Player
entries.title: Player: "“Officially warning them is a possi..."
entries.dialogueText: “Officially warning them is a possibility but isn't tangible, we need action.”
entries.menuText: “Officially warning them is a possibility but isn't tangible, we need action.”

entries.speaker: Player
entries.title: Player: "“You were right. The administration..."
entries.dialogueText: “You were right. The administration won't work with the SSC again.”
entries.menuText: “You were right. The administration won't work with the SSC again.”

entries.speaker: Player
entries.title: Player: "“I need to hear solutions not excus..."
entries.dialogueText: “I need to hear solutions not excuses or reasons.”
entries.menuText: “I need to hear solutions not excuses or reasons.”

entries.speaker: Gus Manger
entries.title: Gus Manger: "“Excuse my bluntness, sir. The mana..."
entries.dialogueText: “Excuse my bluntness, sir. The management of SSC is hard to communicate with because they have the know-it-all attitude.”

entries.speaker: Gus Manger
entries.title: Gus Manger: "“Good call, Mr. President. Underhal..."
entries.dialogueText: “Good call, Mr. President. Underhall should be available for a second project in the future if we have the budget to do it.”

entries.speaker: Symon Holl
entries.title: Symon Holl: "“We must focus on solving the issue..."
entries.dialogueText: “We must focus on solving the issue at hand.”

entries.speaker: Gus Manger
entries.title: Gus Manger: "“You are right. My advice would be..."
entries.dialogueText: “You are right. My advice would be to warn them. There is a chance they might wake up to the situation.”

entries.speaker: Gus Manger
entries.title: Gus Manger: "“I don't know who they will listen..."
entries.dialogueText: “I don't know who they will listen to if they aren't listening to the President of Sordland.”

entries.speaker: Symon Holl
entries.title: Symon Holl: "“It would be possible to demand a c..."
entries.dialogueText: “It would be possible to demand a change in leadership.”

entries.speaker: Gus Manger
entries.title: Gus Manger: "“I expected some issue even before..."
entries.dialogueText: “I expected some issue even before we started this. This corporation is full of fossils that don't know how to solve problems reactively.”
